newsitem.title: UK: IGC lowers 1997 world coarse grains crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: IGC lowers 1997 world coarse grains crop estimate.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday cut its 1997 world coarse grains crop estimate to 896 million tonnes compared with the previous estimate made a month ago of 901 million.
In its Grains Market Report, the IGC put the 1996 crop at 902 million tonnes.

A sharp cut in estimated US production is largely responsible for the fall, with the IGC's estimate cut to 273.4 million tonnes compared with the previous 278.6 million and an estimate of 267.6 million tonnes for 1996.
The estimate for US maize production has been cut by four million tonnes to 246 million, as a result of hot and dry weather in the corn belt, the IGC said.
The IGC's estimates for Russia and Ukraine were both raised by 500,000 tonnes, to 34 million tonnes for Russia and 12.5 million for Ukraine.
There was also a rise of 500,000 tonnes for Sudan, to 4.6 million tonnes, as well as several other small changes. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
